images.title: Six rows of 19 squares in a frame of 20
images.purpose: Show why 6 × 20 counts too many squares: the tray has 6 rows of 19 squares, and the frame of 6 rows of 20 has one missing square in every row, a strip of 6 squares.
images.composition: One array of 6 rows by 20 columns across the middle: the first 19 columns are filled squares and the 20th column is a dashed empty strip, with a bracket and a count above, a bracket and a count at the left, a label under the strip and one line under the picture.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. One array of 6 rows by 20 columns of square positions. Every square is 56 by 56 px with a 4 px gap, so the pitch is 60 px; column k (k = 1 to 20) starts at x = 190 + (k − 1) × 60 and row j (j = 1 to 6) starts at y = 250 + (j − 1) × 60. The array spans x 190 to 1386 and y 250 to 606. Columns 1 to 19 (x 190 to 1326) hold 114 filled squares (6 × 19), each filled amber #E69F00 with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline and rounded corners (radius 6 px). Column 20 (x 1330 to 1386) holds 6 squares of the same size with no fill (white) and a dashed grey #6B7280 outline (dashes 8 px, gaps 6 px): this is the missing strip. In all there are 120 square positions, 114 filled and 6 dashed. Above the filled squares, a thin dark #2B2B2B bracket: a horizontal line at y 228 from x 190 to x 1326 with a 12 px tick at each end pointing down; centred at x 758 and y 192 the label 19 squares in each row (dark #1F2937 sans-serif, 38 px). At the left, a thin dark vertical bracket line at x 168 from y 250 to y 606 with a 12 px tick at each end pointing right; centred at x 95 and y 428 the label 6 rows (38 px). Under the dashed strip, a short grey #6B7280 leader line from x 1358 and y 614 to y 642, and centred at x 1230 and y 668 the label 6 missing squares (38 px). Centred at x 728 and y 752 the caption 6 × 19 = 6 × 20 − 6 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (46 px). No other text and no numbers inside the squares. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a frame with a column count other than 20, or a filled block of any size other than 6 rows by 19 columns
a missing strip that is filled, has a solid outline, or has a number of squares other than 6
images.takeaway: 6 × 20 counts a whole strip of 6 squares that is not there, so 6 × 19 is 6 less than 6 × 20.
images.description: A tray of 6 rows of 19 amber squares with a dashed empty column of 6 squares at the end, showing the squares that 6 × 20 counts by mistake.
images.context: Concept image for Use a Friendly Number, Then Adjust. It follows the idea of the nearest multiple pictures in your maths book (a block of squares with one white strip at the end) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 6 rows of 19.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student count the filled squares in a row (19) and see the empty twentieth square in every row. The slip to watch: rounding to 20 and stopping at 6 × 20 without taking the strip of 6 away.

image_decisions.why: The array with its dashed strip is the mathematics: the strip of 6 missing squares is why 6 × 20 must be reduced by 6.
